intro:
Every marketing agency in South Florida will tell you it can fill your tables. Very few actually understand what it takes to run a restaurant, where the margins are thin, the reviews are public, and a slow Tuesday is a real problem. So when you search for the best restaurant marketing agency in South Florida, the real question is not who has the flashiest website. It is who understands covers, tickets, and repeat visits.

We are Button Up Media, and yes, we put ourselves at number one on this list. We will be straight with you about why, and we will be just as honest about the seven other Miami, Fort Lauderdale, Boca Raton, and Coral Gables agencies below. Several of them are genuinely excellent, and for certain restaurants they may be the better call. This guide lays out what each firm does best so you can pick the right partner, not just the first name you find.

sections.h2: How we ranked these South Florida restaurant marketing agencies
sections.html: We are a restaurant marketing agency ourselves, so we are not pretending to be a neutral review site. Instead, we tried to be useful. Every agency below is a real South Florida firm with genuine restaurant or hospitality experience. For each one we looked at three things: how focused they are on restaurants specifically, what they do best, and the kind of owner they fit. We did not invent stats, awards, or client counts for anyone, including ourselves. Where a firm is a general agency rather than a restaurant specialist, we say so plainly, because for the right owner that is a feature, not a flaw.

sections.h2: 1. Button Up Media (South Florida): best for restaurants
sections.html:
Button Up Media is a marketing agency built for one type of business: restaurants. That is the whole point. We do not split our attention across dentists, law firms, and e-commerce brands. We spend our days inside the specifics of hospitality, which means we already understand slow shoulder seasons, the difference between a reservations problem and a walk-in problem, and why a five-star review streak matters more than a follower count.

Our work connects the channels an owner actually cares about. Paid ads, social media, and websites are built to drive one thing: measurable bookings, phone calls, and online orders. We keep the reporting in plain language, because most owners do not want a dashboard with forty metrics. They want to know if last month's spend put more people in seats.

Are we the right fit for everyone? No. If your single biggest need is a national brand campaign or high-end drone cinematography, some of the specialists below may serve you better. But if you run a South Florida restaurant and you want a team that lives and breathes restaurants, we believe we earn the top spot. Book a free call with Button Up Media and we will tell you honestly whether we are the right partner for your restaurant.

Host Hospitality is a Miami digital marketing agency that works exclusively with restaurants and food-and-beverage brands. Their scope is broad within that niche, covering paid ads, SEO, social media, content, influencer partnerships, and email. They position themselves as a growth partner focused on making F&B brands more visible, recognizable, and profitable.

Best for: established restaurants and F&B brands that want a restaurant-only team running paid ads and social as a full growth engine, rather than piecing together individual services.

Restaurant Suite 360 is a Miami-based agency that serves restaurants exclusively and bundles an unusually wide range of services under one roof: menu design, web design, social media, Google Ads, SEO, online ordering, and photo and video. Their pitch centers on local-first marketing that drives real bookings, calls, and online orders.

Best for: owners who want a single restaurant-focused shop to handle everything from menus and website to ads and ordering, instead of juggling several separate vendors.

Slique Media is a social-media and content creative agency that has long worked with restaurants and hospitality brands. Their specialty is social strategy, short-form and branded content, TikTok, and influencer marketing, with a focus on turning trend-aware content into engagement and loyal customers.

Best for: restaurants that live or die by social content and want strong creative, short-form video, and influencer work at the center of their marketing.

William Davis Moore is a visual media and social studio serving Palm Beach and Broward counties. They produce restaurant photography, video, and drone content alongside social media management, framing the work as restaurant marketing that turns attention into reservations.

Best for: Palm Beach and Broward restaurants that primarily need high-quality food and venue photo and video, plus day-to-day social management to go with it.

Savage Global Marketing is a Fort Lauderdale creative and advertising agency offering advertising, social media, web development, and video production. Their restaurant experience includes a Taco Bell Cantina case study, and they lean on bold creative and an all-in-one production approach.

Best for: Broward-area restaurants that want a general creative agency with strong production and advertising chops, rather than a restaurant-only niche shop.

Ardor Consulting is a Miami marketing and branding firm offering brand strategy, influencer marketing, web design, SEO, social media, and fractional CMO services, with hospitality and restaurants among the sectors it serves. Its approach centers on storytelling that builds trust and authority.

Best for: restaurant groups or growing concepts that want brand strategy and senior marketing direction, not just channel-by-channel execution.

Heyday Marketing is a Coral Gables full-service digital agency offering SEO, PPC, social media, email, content, branding, and web design, and it lists restaurants among the industries it serves. It positions itself as bringing big-brand strategy to small and mid-sized businesses with no long-term contracts.

Best for: restaurants that want a broad, data-driven digital agency and value month-to-month flexibility over a restaurant-only specialist.

sections.h2: How to choose the right restaurant marketing agency for your restaurant
sections.html:
Start with the problem, not the agency. If you cannot fill tables and you want everything tied to real results, a restaurant-only team like Button Up Media, Host Hospitality, or Restaurant Suite 360 is the natural starting point. If your food looks flat online, a visual studio like William Davis Moore or a social specialist like Slique Media may move the needle faster. If you are launching a new concept or rebranding, Ardor Consulting's brand strategy focus fits. And if you want big-agency breadth without a long contract, Heyday Marketing and Savage Global Marketing are worth a conversation.

Then ask three questions on any intro call. Do you work with restaurants specifically, or are we one industry among many? How will you measure success, and will I understand the reporting? And what does month three look like if this is working? An honest agency will give you clear answers. If you want ours, book a free call with Button Up Media and we will walk you through exactly how we would approach your restaurant.

faqs.q: What is the best restaurant marketing agency in South Florida?
faqs.a: For most independent restaurants, we believe Button Up Media is the best restaurant marketing agency in South Florida, because it works only with restaurants and ties ads, social, and web to bookings, calls, and orders. That said, Host Hospitality and Restaurant Suite 360 in Miami are strong restaurant-focused alternatives, and the right pick depends on what your restaurant needs most.

faqs.q: Are there restaurant marketing agencies that work only with restaurants?
faqs.a: Yes. Button Up Media, Host Hospitality, and Restaurant Suite 360 all focus specifically on restaurants and food-and-beverage brands. Working with a restaurant-only agency usually means less time spent explaining how your business works and more time on strategy built for hospitality.

faqs.q: Which South Florida agency is best for social media and short-form video?
faqs.a: Slique Media in Miami specializes in social strategy, short-form and branded content, TikTok, and influencer marketing, which makes it a strong fit for restaurants where social content drives most of their traffic. William Davis Moore in Boca Raton is another option when you need photo and video plus day-to-day social.

faqs.q: Who should I use for restaurant photography and video in Palm Beach or Broward?
faqs.a: William Davis Moore is a visual media and social studio serving Palm Beach and Broward counties, producing restaurant photography, video, and drone content alongside social management. For bold creative and full production in the Fort Lauderdale area, Savage Global Marketing is also worth considering.

faqs.q: Is a restaurant-specialist agency better than a general marketing agency?
faqs.a: It depends on your goal. A restaurant specialist understands covers, reviews, and seasonality out of the gate, which is why we lead with restaurant-only firms. But a general agency like Heyday Marketing or Savage Global Marketing can be the better choice if you want broad digital services, flexible contracts, or heavy creative production that goes beyond a restaurant niche.

faqs.q: I need brand strategy, not just ads. Who fits?
faqs.a: Ardor Consulting in Miami offers brand strategy, fractional CMO services, and senior marketing direction, with hospitality among the sectors it serves. It is a good fit for restaurant groups or growing concepts that need higher-level direction rather than only channel execution.

faqs.q: Do these agencies require long-term contracts?
faqs.a: It varies by firm, so always confirm during your intro call. Heyday Marketing, for example, positions itself around no long-term contracts and month-to-month flexibility. If contract terms matter to you, ask each agency directly before you sign anything.
